# NI03 Pending-only source checkpoint

Historical source checkpoint at `7d3f3aa`. The successor [retained Pending recovery and request-retry checkpoint](native-ni03-retained-recovery.md) implements and validates the bounded recovery/retry paths that were still absent here. The results and limits below describe this predecessor.

Status: integrated partial source implementation. The formatted 323-file candidate passes all 1,018 workspace tests with zero failures and one existing opt-in workflow ignore, plus formatting and the ordinary workspace build. The corrected focused run passes all eight Pending tests. The earlier five-pass/three-fail source, full output and executable remain preserved under `native-ni03-public8-first-failure-20261016`, manifest `45d5647089d5abcb2e57724c2b849d9ade1ca7aeb600bbbcfa20a5d072377d8c`. Only inconsistent fixtures and a pruning-sensitive oracle were repaired; standard rustfmt changed three files before full validation. No production check or authority boundary was relaxed. This is not full NI03 completion or installed qualification. Strict workspace/all-target Clippy also passes after expressing the test quota values directly in their struct initializer; values and assertions are unchanged. The full-suite source and original lint failure remain retained.

The private `PendingIssuer` is selected at trusted startup with actual Wallet/Native/key/journal sources, a Native startup pin and a maximum lifetime of 1–60 seconds. Its incoming method accepts only exact request bytes. It acquires the real Wallet lease, Native current lease and held policy; fixes one issue time from the existing Native OS clock; and validates complete candidate windows in descending order to choose the largest admitted lifetime under the startup cap. Longer rejected candidates are never signed or persisted. Native policy/key/holder/permission/receiver/descriptor/future-deny and Wallet bounds are checked before entropy or a private-key lease. Revalidation retains the same original window, policy observation and raw request.

The actual descriptor must have empty required credentials, required capabilities and accepted evidence, and no required authority mode. The unchanged typed no-required-evidence preparation binds its finite original observation, Native owner epoch, descriptor, holder, request and source profile. An unsupported obligation denies; this source does not establish that any deployed descriptor is eligible for the none branch or qualify any external evidence adapter.

The retained `PreparedServiceIntent` supplies request/operation/resource/opcode/handler/fingerprint facts. Holder and issuer facts come from the held Wallet reference and selected Native issuer. OS CSPRNG failures, zero identity groups after at most four attempts and journal uniqueness collisions deny. No caller supplies challenge IDs, sessions, nonces, issue/expiry values, policy, audience, subject or key selectors. A journal collision exports nothing; durable retry identity/rebinding is deliberately not implemented by this increment.

The private concrete guard explicitly borrows the Wallet lease as well as Native policy and the actual issuer-key lease. It compares the exact original challenge/signature/request, evidence bytes and existing Wallet lineage; recomputes the full request preparation with the same held policy/window/observation; and strictly verifies the original issuer signature against the selected held key. It checks actual current sources and full active windows again. It accepts only Pending with empty packet/context and zero completion timestamps. Complete and Cached deny. The existing journal reserves and persists Pending, closes storage under its lock and repeats the full guard at its durable clock floor before the signed challenge can return. The private clock adapter uses the existing Native OS clock, rejects rollback/failure and cannot clear a prior clock error.

The production code changes are confined to the private composition, retaining the already-created typed intent, and removing the three consumed method-local dead-code expectations. The private Pending composition remains separate from absent completion/context/admission. Public module visibility, generic/human contracts, wire schemas, dependencies/locks, evidence logic, journal logic, issuer method bodies, Wallet presentation denials, fixtures/goldens and business scheduling remain unchanged.

The additive regression source still contains eight test functions. The preceding revision ran with five passes and three failures; the corrected eight tests below now pass in both their focused run and the full workspace:

- Both Runtime and Service profiles: actual public Wallet metadata, actual Native/key leases and guard, independently verified issuer signature, fixture-derived operation/resource/opcode/handler/descriptor/schema/holder-public-key claims and all five original evidence times. The existing ordinary post-close callback attempts exclusive Wallet/Native/key locks during the original issuance call, with explicit WouldBlock/EWOULDBLOCK-or-EAGAIN contention checks and an external reached assertion. Reopened durable Pending and the original later-guard exclusion checks remain separate assertions; they do not claim restart/rebinding support.
- All four external-obligation surfaces: a real active Wallet reference first accepts an unchanged next-generation configuration, then each isolated nonempty obligation requires exact Wallet configuration `Invalid` denial. Separate pure `prepare_none` controls require exact `UnsupportedRequiredEvidence`. The current Wallet contract prevents admitting such a current state, so this does not claim that the end-to-end PendingIssuer unsupported-evidence branch ran. No key lease or journal issuance is invoked in this configuration test; existing evidence controls remain unchanged.
- Largest pre-sign original windows: startup maximum, Native/issuer/holder/permission/principal validity, receiver cap and future deny. The Native-policy and receiver-principal cases explicitly co-bound holder, Wallet and enclosing policy validity as required by the original current-source contract; the exact original TTL expectations remain 11 and 15 seconds. This covers the consistent joint bound, not independent narrowing of otherwise inconsistent metadata.
- Exact claim/request/signature/evidence/lineage substitutions, Complete/Cached, completion fields and changed current Native epoch.
- Startup pin mismatch, invalid startup caps, ordinary Wallet lock contention and journal pending quota, with no new challenge returned on denial.
- Existing ordinary post-close clock fixture: assert the hook ran and issuance returned exact `Journal(Expired)` with no challenge. A read-only SQLite query before any later journal session requires the persisted tombstone row and durable deadline; the subsequent stats session must prune the expired row and return exact zero counts. No private backend-error/fault/interposer hook is introduced or used.
- Sticky Native clock rollback and failure.
- Current issuer revocation, malformed raw request and a supported ordinary Wallet metadata-fixture transition to a new inactive current reference.

The disposable issuer seed `[81; 32]` is explicit public test material already used by the predecessor's issuer fixtures. The metadata fixture's sentinel Wallet seed does not establish Wallet private seed health. Existing fixture/golden bytes and pre-existing tests are unchanged. The preceding source compiled successfully; its three failed assertions are retained as failed evidence. This corrected test revision passed ordinary focused and workspace validation. The earlier positive test passed both-profile claims/horizons and original-call lease checks; that pass is bounded to the earlier source tuple. The retained NI02 default seven-command driver has a 10 GiB initial external-stage free-space floor (`preparation/inputs.json`, `minimum_external_available_bytes=10737418240`); that historical driver and floor remain unchanged. Its release explicitly says this is not a product or guest minimum. The first ordinary filtered command used a fresh clone-only target, an offline registry, one job and a 0.25-second disk watchdog; observed volume consumption was 307,617,792 bytes and minimum available space was 1,458,577,408 bytes. Its owned group was empty and child reaped. The corrected source was rerun after inactive compiler-cache cleanup; no VM requirement was introduced.

Still open: full NI03 restart/reacquisition/rebinding and durable idempotent retry, NI05 completion/cache/context, qualified nonempty external evidence, Wallet C and holder presentation, NI01 and installed/artifact-bound Native admission, live key role/descriptor/target provisioning and Gate exit. Neither this checkpoint nor ordinary public fixture source provides execution authority or production qualification.

Coverage limits remain explicit: these eight authored tests do not independently mutate every evidence-time/digest field, exercise dropped-owner compiler denials, all holder/Wallet revocation/expiry combinations or Service post-close expiry, inject entropy/identity collisions/storage errors, or qualify restart/rebinding. Existing tests remain preserved; the explicit workspace result covers their actual execution without expanding the listed coverage claims. The post-close callback uses only the existing ordinary public-fixture hook; no private fault/interposer/backend-error path is added or invoked.
